findings.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), silently altering light-theme rendering instead of only adding a dark-theme alternative. Users on light themes get noticeably lighter (lower-contrast) usernames in the small-action row than before this PR; the stated goal was to change only dark-theme colors, so light-theme users are bitten by an unintended visual regression.

[BUG] .custom-message-length light branch was inverted from $lightness: 70% to $lightness: 30%. Mobile light-theme users see the custom-message-length hint text at 30% lightness (much darker, near-primary) instead of the previous muted 70%, contradicting the PR's stated intent of only changing dark-theme colors.

[BUG] The h3 light branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). Mobile light-theme users see linked-preview h3 titles at half the previous contrast; a light-theme regression outside the PR's stated scope.

[BUG] The .name light branch was changed from $lightness: 30% to $lightness: 50%, making both branches of dark-light-choose identical. Desktop light-theme user-card names render at 50% lightness instead of the previous 30%, and the now-duplicated arguments show the change was not the intended mechanical mirror — light-theme users get a visual regression.

[BUG] The .name light branch was changed from $lightness: 30% to $lightness: 50%, identical to the dark branch. Mobile light-theme user-card names lose the previous 30%-lightness styling; unintended light-theme regression duplicating the dark value.

[BUG] embed.css.scss now calls dark-light-choose, a function defined in the common stylesheet foundation (colors/functions partials) that the embed stylesheet pipeline may not import. If the embed stylesheet is compiled as a standalone entry point without the partial defining dark-light-choose (as it was before, since it only used built-in scale-color), Sass compilation of /embed stylesheet fails with 'undefined function dark-light-choose', breaking embedded topics entirely.

[ADVISORY] The mirrored lightness values (e.g. 70% -> 30%) assume $primary and $secondary are always inverting counterparts, but scale-color with $lightness is not symmetric when secondaries have different saturation/chroma. Dark-theme admins who customize $secondary to a saturated hue get heatmap/heatmap-cold text at arbitrary effective contrast rather than the intended mirror; bitten when a custom dark color scheme is selected.

[BUG] The light-theme branch lightness was silently changed from 30% to 70% while converting to dark-light-choose, breaking the light theme. In light themes, the small-action link color becomes scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) — a washed-out near-background tone instead of the intended strong 30% dark tone — so links in small-action rows lose contrast and readability for all light-theme users; only the dark branch (30%) matches the pattern used elsewhere in this diff.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for the h3 (topic title in onebox/small-action block) was changed from 20% to 50% lightness during conversion. Mobile light-theme users see the onebox/topic h3 heading at 50% lightness (muted gray) instead of the previous near-black 20%, silently weakening the visual hierarchy of titles; the sibling desktop rule kept 20%, so mobile and desktop now diverge.

[BUG] The light branch for .name changed from 30% to 50% lightness, and it now matches the adjacent .title instead of staying distinct. On the desktop user profile, the user's display name loses its previous darker emphasis in light themes (30% → 50%), making the name indistinguishable from the title text below it; this is a behavioral change to light theme beyond the stated dark-theme scope.

[BUG] The light branch for .name changed from 30% to 50% lightness during conversion, mirroring the desktop regression. Mobile light-theme users see the profile display name at the same muted 50% lightness as the title, losing the previous emphasis; light-theme rendering changed even though the PR claims to only fix dark themes.

[BUG] The light branch for .custom-message-length was changed from 70% to 30% lightness, inverting the intended dimness in light themes. Mobile light-theme users see the character-count hint at 30% lightness (nearly full-strength text) instead of the previous subtle 70% dim tone, and the dark branch (70%) now renders the hint fainter than the light branch — the polarity is backwards relative to every other conversion in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The heatmap sibling rules (.heatmap-high/med/low) on the same color-temperature path use hardcoded #fe7a15 orange and are not converted, leaving them broken on dark themes. Dark-theme users get the same low-contrast rendering problem for heatmap cells that coldmap cells got fixed for; if the coldmap→secondary conversion was required, the adjacent heatmap half of the same temperature-map component was silently dropped from scope.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of the colorspace was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), which is not the mechanical 100-L inversion the PR title promises. Light-theme users see the small-action links in post rows rendered at 70% lightness of $primary (near-white) instead of the previous darker 30% tone — a light-mode regression completely unrelated to the stated 'fix dark themes' intent; nobody asked for the light branch to change here.

[BUG] .custom-message-length light branch was changed from $primary lightness 70% to $primary lightness 30%, altering light-theme styling rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. Light-theme mobile users see the custom-message character counter become a dark 30%-lightness color where it was previously a muted 70%-lightness color — visible light-mode regression untraceable to the 'use $secondary for dark themes' requirement.

[BUG] The .name light branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), and the result is identical to the .title rule directly below it, so the light-mode hierarchy between name and title is erased. On light themes the user-card name loses its previous visual distinction from the title (both now 50%), a light-mode behavior change with no requirement behind it; also inconsistent with common/base/user.scss where .name keeps 30%.

[BUG] Mobile .name light branch changed from 30% to 50% lightness of $primary, matching .title and diverging from the desktop/common counterparts that retain 30%. Mobile light-theme user cards lose name/title contrast and drift out of sync with common/base/user.scss (.name stays at 30%), producing inconsistent appearance across mobile and desktop for the same element.

[BUG] The h3 light branch was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), a light-mode change that is neither the 100-L inversion (would be 80%) nor traceable to the stated intent. Mobile light-theme link-preview titles become significantly lighter than before and inconsistent with desktop/topic-post.scss line 318 which keeps the 20% light branch, so the same element renders differently on mobile vs desktop light themes.

[ADVISORY] dark-light-choose() is used in the embed stylesheet, whose compilation pipeline is separate from the main theme stylesheets and does not include the dark/light scheme context the function depends on. Embedded comments are rendered with whatever single colorset the embed build compiles against; if dark-light-choose (or $secondary) is not defined for the embed pipeline the stylesheet fails to compile, and if it is defined it resolves to a single fixed choice, making this hunk a no-op or a build break rather than the dark-theme fix it claims to be.

[ADVISORY] The coldmap classes use three distinct lightness steps (70/60/50) whose dark-theme counterparts (30/40/50) converge such that coldmap-low's dark value equals the 50% used everywhere else, flattening the intended 'colder = dimmer' gradient in dark mode. In dark themes the heat-map age gradient becomes nearly indistinguishable from ordinary muted text, degrading the information the coldmap encodes; a staff reviewer would ask whether the dark values were derived from a contrast check or just mirrored.

[BUG] The dark-theme conversion silently changes the light-theme value: .custom-message-length was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) and becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), ...), dropping the light branch from 70% to 30%. Light-theme users see the custom message length counter change from a faint 70%-lightness gray to a near-full-contrast 30% color — an unintended visual regression on mobile modals; the desktop twin (desktop/modal.scss:91) keeps 70%, so mobile and desktop now diverge.

[BUG] The conversion changes the light-theme value: .user-card / h3 was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) and becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...), altering the light branch from 20% to 50%. Mobile user-card headings (topic poster names in quoted cards) render at 50% lightness instead of 20% on light themes — visibly lighter text — while the desktop equivalent (desktop/topic-post.scss:318) keeps 20%, producing a desktop/mobile visual drift introduced by this mechanical refactor.

[BUG] The conversion changes the light-theme value: the nested a was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)), changing the light branch from 30% to 70%. Desktop reply/usernames in this block drop from near-full-contrast (30%) to a faint 70% tint on light themes, harming legibility; the parallel mobile rule (mobile/topic-post.scss, .username a) correctly keeps 30%, so the two layouts now disagree.

[BUG] The conversion changes the light-theme value: .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...), altering the light branch from 30% to 50%. The user-profile display name on desktop light themes becomes 20 lightness-points fainter than before the refactor, an unintended change bundled into what the PR title describes as a dark-theme-only fix.

[BUG] The conversion changes the light-theme value: .name was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...), altering the light branch from 30% to 50%. Mobile user-profile display names on light themes become fainter (50% vs 30% lightness) with no dark-theme justification, and now match neither the pre-refactor value nor the .title element styled three lines below, flattening the intended name/title hierarchy.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), drifting beyond the PR's stated intent of only adding a $secondary variant for dark themes. In light themes, usernames in the small-action/post-notice block render at 70% lightness instead of 30% — near-invisible washed-out text where the pre-PR design was dark and high-contrast; a user-visible regression the PR title never asked for and no reviewer accepted.

[BUG] The light-theme argument of .custom-message-length was changed from 70% to 30% lightness, contradicting the parallel desktop/modal.scss:94 hunk which keeps 70%. Mobile users in light themes see the custom-message-length hint at 30% lightness (heavy, near-black) while desktop sees the intended 70% (subtle grey), producing inconsistent, unapproved visual drift on mobile only.

[BUG] The .name rule's light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50% lightness while the adjacent .title kept its original 50%, flattening the intended hierarchy in light themes. User profile names lose their darker, bolder styling relative to titles in light themes — a deliberate visual hierarchy removed without any requirement in the PR asking for it.

[BUG] Same silent light-theme change as desktop: .name went from 30% to 50% lightness, matching .title and erasing the previous hierarchy. Mobile light-theme profile names render at the same grey as titles, losing the 30%-vs-50% contrast the original design encoded.

[BUG] The h3 rule's light-theme branch was changed from 20% to 50% lightness, while the equivalent desktop/topic-post.scss:321 hunk correctly preserves 20%. Mobile light-theme users see topic link titles at 50% (washed-out grey) instead of the desktop's 20% (dark heading), diverging mobile from desktop and from the original accepted design.

[ADVISORY] The light-mode branch was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), not just wrapped in dark-light-choose. Light-theme users see the small-action link color jump from a dark 30% to a washed-out 70% lightness — a user-visible regression the PR description (dark themes only) does not authorize; same pattern at mobile/topic-post.scss:182 (20%→50%), mobile/modal.scss:102 (70%→30%), desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 (.name 30%→50%).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] dark-light-choose() is used in the embed stylesheet, whose compilation pipeline is separate from the main theme stylesheets and does not include the dark/light scheme context the function depends on. Embedded comments are rendered with whatever single colorset the embed build compiles against; if dark-light-choose (or $secondary) is not defined for the embed pipeline the stylesheet fails to compile, and if it is defined it resolves to a single fixed choice, making this hunk a no-op or a build break rather than the dark-theme fix it claims to be.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` to use `dark-light-choose(...)` and references `$secondary` (e.g., `a.new-user { color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)); }`). If the embed stylesheet is compiled in a context where `dark-light-choose` and/or `$secondary` are not available (or where dark/light scheme switching isn't meaningful), this change could either fail compilation or resolve to a single fixed color. However, the claim about a separate embed compilation pipeline and missing scheme context is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The coldmap classes use three distinct lightness steps (70/60/50) whose dark-theme counterparts (30/40/50) converge such that coldmap-low's dark value equals the 50% used everywhere else, flattening the intended 'colder = dimmer' gradient in dark mode. In dark themes the heat-map age gradient becomes nearly indistinguishable from ordinary muted text, degrading the information the coldmap encodes; a staff reviewer would ask whether the dark values were derived from a contrast check or just mirrored.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/discourse.scss`, the `.coldmap-high/med/low` colors were changed to `dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30/40/50%))`. This does make the dark-theme palette for the coldmap explicitly 30/40/50 on `$secondary`, and `50%` is also used widely elsewhere in the diff for muted/default text colors, so it’s reasonable to flag a potential loss of visual distinction/gradient strength in dark mode. However, the diff alone can’t verify the claim that the gradient becomes “nearly indistinguishable” or that contrast wasn’t checked, and it’s a UX/theming concern rather than a functional defect.
